The iPhone Duo, which launched last month to mixed reviews, contains a range of technological feats and breakthroughs. One of these is its nano-texture interior screen, which contrasts with the glossy outer screen and helps to conceal the crease that marred so many early (and a fair few more recent) foldable phones.

The Duo has been out for a couple of weeks now, which means the repairs site iFixit has had time to perform its usual thorough teardown. And among other discoveries, the team have shed light on how that screen texture works, and how it bears comparisons to the matt finishes on rival products. Spoiler: it compares very well.

In a post to Twitter/X this week, iFixit discussed this aspect of the teardown. The site used an Evident DSX2000 microscope at increasing magnifications to examine the Duo’s nano-texture screen, along with two other matte surfaces: the screen of an e-ink reader and “a popular matte screen protector film.”

“At low magnification,” iFixit reports, “the difference is clear. The e-ink texture blurs everything underneath. The matt protector softens the pixels. The nanotexture lets far more detail through.”

As the site points out, sharp detail isn’t as much of a priority for an e-ink reader as it is for a smartphone, which may explain why the respective makers would be satisfied with this functional difference. But it doesn’t explain what physical qualities produce the difference. That is explained at higher magnification.

“The nanotexture’s pattern is much smaller and more defined than the protector’s,” the tweet reports, backing this up with photographic evidence. The e-ink reader, by contrast, has a “pillowy texture” which is “huge by comparison.”

The photos are clear. The Duo’s screen features a tight pattern of what look like cells or tiny bubbles, while the screen protector has a swampy, uneven pattern and the e-ink reader features massive polygons.

There’s a real difference here. “Is the iPhone Duo’s nano-texture just a matt screen protector with fancy Apple marketing?” iFixit asks, before concluding: “Verdict: not just marketing.”

What’s even better is that nano-texure layer is easy to replace. If you have AppleCare+, Apple charges just $19 to replace it when it when it gets worn down.

Apple’s new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display isn’t just the best display ever put in a laptop. It’s also Apple’s first-ever touchscreen in a Mac and the first time macOS has supported Touch as an input option. It’s a feature we longtime Mac users thought we’d never see, mostly because Apple has a history of saying it won’t happen.

But it has happened—and on the expensive laptop Apple sells, no less. While the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display has plenty of other features to attract customers, which I will outline in my upcoming review, the touchscreen is one of the most interesting features to come to the Mac in years and is sure to be a major consideration for buyers when choosing which laptop to get.

However, macOS with Touch isn’t the same interface that you can just reach out to control with your fingers. Apple has enhanced and optimized macOS to accommodate Touch, making the overall experience satisfying. Here are my observations after spending a few days with it.

No lag or delay

Apple did not simply take a Touch input sensor, slap it on top of the OLED, pack it all up, and ship it. For the optimal experience, the Touch sensor is incorporated into the OLED panel, just as it is with the iPad Pro. That makes it perform more like a tablet than a usual touchscreen laptop.

Roman Loyola/Foundry

It also means there’s no lag when touching the screen. Tap the screen, and you’ll get an instant reaction from macOS: buttons, menus, sliders, icons, the Dock, you name it. Everything reacts the instant you touch it.

UI clarity

My major concern about the touchscreen MacBook Pro was whether Apple would do enough (or anything) to adjust macOS’s longstanding UI elements for Touch input. Some elements in macOS need to be larger to make them easier to touch; others need to be shifted to create more space; and still others need a complete rethink. A touch UI that demands cursor-style precision means you have to concentrate to do the most mundane of tasks. That’s tiring.

Foundry

In macOS 27.2 on the new MacBook Pro, Apple has enhanced macOS to accommodate Touch. Throughout the OS, elements appear when using Touch and return to the normal view when using a mouse or trackpad. The first thing you’ll notice is the set of traffic lights that appear in the upper right corner of windows to close, minimize, or expand windows full-screen, respectively. When tapped, the red, yellow, and green buttons magnify to make the target easier to hit.

Even menu items adjust by expanding a bit to add space between the items so they’re easier to tap with your finger. Another example is checkboxes, which let you tap on the accompanying text to select as well as the box itself.

Roman Loyola/Foundry

UI confusion

Almost all of the time, I can navigate through macOS just by using Touch. Apple thoughtfully considered the elements that I encountered to make them easy to touch, with one exception: video files. The ability to watch a tiny version of the video by clicking on the “Play” icon in the center of the video’s icon gets in the way of opening the file. Double-tapping to open the video file often resulted in the video playing in the icon, not actually opening the file. It’s one of the things that hasn’t been adjusted to accommodate Touch, and it needs a retool.

I also found that the mindset for Touch on macOS is separate from iOS. My experience with Apple’s touch-based UI is mostly with iOS, so I thought that macOS Touch would work similarly. But Apple decided to stick to macOS conventions, as illustrated by opening an app. In iOS, opening an app is a single tap. When is the best carrier upgrade timing?

Apple typically announces new iPhone models in September. Carriers often roll out their most aggressive trade-in offers and promotional deals around this time to entice customers to upgrade.

New releases: Waiting for the September (or spring) launch window is generally a good strategy if you want the latest model at a potentially better subsidized price.

Check your contract cycle: Many carrier contracts today last 24 to 36 months. If you’re nearing the end of your contract, you’re in a strong position to negotiate or take advantage of upgrade offers. When does Apple update the iPhone?

Apple typically unveils new iPhones at a dedicated Apple event in September. Preorders usually open the following Friday, with devices shipping and arriving in stores a week later. However, some models arrive later: Apple announced the iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max and iPhone Duo in September 2026, but the Pro models went on sale September 18, while the Duo followed on October 23.

Apple also launches iPhones earlier in the year, particularly its more affordable models. The iPhone 16e arrived in February 2025 and the iPhone 17e in March 2026. The standard iPhone 18, iPhone 18e and iPhone Air 2 are expected in spring 2027.

When do iPhone prices drop and by how much?

Based on past experience, Apple is very unlikely to reduce the price of a new iPhone during its first year on sale.

However, when Apple introduces a new generation of iPhones, it usually cuts the price of the previous year’s models. That means September has traditionally been the point when older iPhones become cheaper.

Apple also tends to keep launch prices broadly similar from one generation to the next, at least in the U.S., although exchange rates and other regional factors can affect pricing elsewhere.

Apple’s first foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo, went on sale on October 23, but getting hold of one could prove difficult. Preorders opened on October 16 and delivery estimates slipped rapidly, with Macworld’s U.S. tracking showing waits stretching to January 25, 2027 within around half an hour. Apple is still accepting orders and made limited stock available to walk-in customers at Apple Stores in the U.S., U.K. and other selected markets on October 23.

However, the launch has brought durability concerns, with some early owners reporting cracks and bright lines on the inner display. On October 26, Apple acknowledged an inner-display issue affecting a small number of iPhone Duo units and advised affected customers to contact AppleCare for a replacement. The cause and failure rate remain unclear. Our iPhone Duo fold problems section below explains Apple’s response and what affected owners should do. The underlying cause of the reported screen cracks has not been confirmed.

The Duo opens like a book from a compact 5.4-inch phone into a much larger 7.6-inch device. Apple describes the internal screen as its largest-ever iPhone display, with 50 percent more screen area than the iPhone 18 Pro Max, while the outer display provides more than 90 percent of the screen area of an iPhone 18 Pro. The biggest difference compared to previous iPhones is the folding design, but Apple has done more than simply add a hinge. The iPhone Duo launched with iOS 27.1, which adapts to different positions and orientations with fold-specific interface and multitasking features. These include Split View, hands-free FaceTime and video, StandBy without charging, and layouts that move seamlessly between the two screens. The iOS 27.2 update, released on October 26, adds Apple Pencil (USB-C) support and Edge Light, which uses the display to light your face during video calls.

The other major changes are the 7.6-inch nano-texture inner display, Touch ID replacing Face ID, an A20 Pro processor with vapor-chamber cooling, and a dual-battery system designed around the two halves of the phone. Apple has also introduced camera features that exploit the second screen, including Duo Preview, Smart Take, Kid Cue and Duo FaceTime. Much of the pre-launch reporting proved accurate: the Duo name, book-style design, roughly 7.7- and 5.4-inch screens, Touch ID, two 48MP rear cameras, two front-facing cameras, A20 Pro, C2 modem, MagSafe and the white/dark-blue colors were all anticipated.

iPhone Duo at a glance

  • Apple’s first folding iPhone, with 5.4-inch outer and 7.6-inch inner displays.
  • Touch ID replaces Face ID, with the fingerprint sensor incorporated into the side button.
  • A20 Pro with vapor-chamber cooling, including a new 2nm manufacturing process.
  • Dual-battery architecture, giving up to 44 hours of video playback on the outer display.
  • Fold-specific iOS and camera features, including Split View, Duo Preview, Smart Take, Kid Cue and hands-free use.

iPhone Duo: Top 10 features

The October 23 launch covers more than 70 countries and regions, including the U.S. and U.K., with another 28 markets following on October 30. The Duo will also be available through Apple Stores, selected carriers and authorized retailers, although availability varies by market.

As of October 23, Apple was quoting January 22, 2027 for delivery of the 256GB iPhone Duo in the U.S. and January 25, 2027 in the U.K. Estimates can change and depend on the configuration and delivery location.

Long delivery waits therefore reflect the balance between demand and available supply, rather than revealing how many phones Apple has sold.

iPhone Duo design: What does it look like?

Britta O’Boyle/Foundry

The iPhone Duo uses a book-style folding design. Closed, it is unusually short and wide for an iPhone, measuring 84.1mm wide, 117.8mm tall and 11.3mm thick. Open it and the width expands to 164.6mm, while thickness reduces to just 5.2mm, making it Apple’s thinnest iPhone when unfolded (taking that mantle from the iPhone Air). It weighs 254g.

The outer screen measures 5.4 inches, while the folding inner panel measures 7.6 inches. Both are Super Retina XDR OLED displays with ProMotion up to 120Hz, Always-On display support and up to 3,000 nits outdoor peak brightness. The internal display also has a nano-texture surface designed to reduce reflections and make the crease less noticeable. The inner display also has a replaceable top cover layer.

According to iFixit’s report on Apple’s U.S. repair pricing, replacing the inner screen’s cover layer costs $49 without AppleCare+, or a $19 service fee with AppleCare+. This replaces only the top cover layer. Repairing damage to the inner display itself costs substantially more: $999 without AppleCare+, or a $99 service fee with AppleCare+. If damage is experienced and found to be a manufacturing fault, Apple may accept the device for repair under warranty at no cost.

The frame and hinge cover are made from Grade 5 titanium. Apple uses a mirror-polished finish on the enclosure and a micro-blasted finish on the 3D-printed hinge cover. Ceramic Shield protects the rear, while Ceramic Shield 2 protects the outer display. The phone retains an IP68 rating despite its folding construction.

Britta O’Boyle/Foundry

There are just two colors: Star White and Night Sky, essentially confirming the pre-event reports of silver/white and a very dark blue. For more information read about the iPhone Duo colors.

Action button and Camera Control

There is Camera Control, giving access to exposure, depth, zoom, cameras, styles and tone. It can also launch the new Siri Camera mode.

However, Apple’s Duo doesn’t feature an Action button. The regular iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max retain both the Action button and Camera Control, so this is one hardware-control compromise of the folding model.

Accessories

Apple is also launching two dedicated accessories for the foldable:

  • The iPhone Duo Case at $79/£79
  • The Duo Folio with Kickstand at $129/£129

Apple’s standard case leaves the hinge exposed, while the Folio with Kickstand provides hinge protection.

Both became available to order on October 16. And there are plenty more of the best cases for iPhone Duo in our test reviews.

iPhone Duo problems: Screen cracks and hinge concerns

Some early iPhone Duo owners have reported cracks along the inner display’s fold, sometimes accompanied by bright lines across the screen. One Australian owner said the damage appeared after around six hours and fewer than 20 openings, and reported receiving an immediate replacement at an Apple Store. These are owner reports; the cause and extent of the problem remain unclear.

Apple acknowledged the issue on October 26, saying it affects a small number of iPhone Duo units. The company advises customers experiencing inner-display problems to contact AppleCare for a replacement. Apple has not announced a formal repair program or confirmed the underlying cause. As reported on November 2, Apple has also circulated diagnostic guidance to Apple Stores and Apple Authorized Service Providers. Read our report on the Duo’s display and hinge problems.

iFixit’s teardown offers a possible explanation: its 3D hinge model places reported damage near a transition between the flex-cable opening and central display support. One simulation shows how a support that fails to retract sufficiently could press against the folding screen.

Apple published an iPhone Duo hinge troubleshooting guide on October 23. It covers devices that do not open or close fully, unexpected noises, loose or damaged hinges, and enclosure damage affecting the mechanism.

Apple says there are no software remedies for hinge problems, so restarting, updating or restoring the phone is unnecessary. Its service procedure calls for inspection and, if the problem remains unresolved, replacement of the inner display assembly. Owners experiencing problems should contact Apple or an authorized service provider for assessment.

How repairable is the iPhone Duo?

iFixit awarded the Duo a provisional repairability score of 5/10, its highest for a foldable at the time. It praised the removable outer display and electrically released batteries, but found inner-display and hinge repairs difficult. The score reflects some accessible components, but is provisional pending replacement-parts availability.

Its fluorescent-powder experiment also found particles reaching the hinge, but this does not establish the cause of owners’ screen failures.

Face ID, Touch ID and the notch

Britta O’Boyle/Foundry

Perhaps the most surprising difference between the iPhone Duo and Apple’s other flagship iPhones is that there is no Face ID.

Instead, Apple has brought back Touch ID, with the fingerprint sensor incorporated into the side button. It works whether the Duo is folded or unfolded, and Apple Watch can also be used to unlock the device. This confirms one of the most persistent pre-launch rumors.

The internal display therefore does not need the TrueDepth sensors used for Face ID. Its FaceTime camera sits beneath the display and disappears when it isn’t being used, giving the inner screen a largely uninterrupted surface.

The inner camera itself is hidden below the display rather than sitting permanently in a visible camera cutout. And yet, despite this and the absence of Face ID, there is still support for Dynamic Island.

Future Duo models could restore Face ID. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Apple has tested iPhone Duo 2 prototypes with an under-display Face ID sensor and camera on the outer screen. However, he suggests the technology could arrive with either the second or third generation, so its inclusion in the next model remains uncertain.

iPhone Duo cameras: What cameras does it have?

Britta O’Boyle/Foundry

The Duo has a 48MP Dual Fusion camera system, comprising:

The Duo does not have variable aperture. Variable aperture is exclusive to the 48MP Fusion Main camera in the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.

The biggest camera features for iPhone Duo

Duo Preview

The outer screen can show a live preview while somebody else is being photographed, allowing the subject to adjust their pose and framing.

Smart Take and Kid Cue

Smart Take detects when everybody is ready and automatically captures the shot. Kid Cue uses animations on the outer screen to encourage children to look towards the camera.

Two-screen shooting

The folding design supports unusual shooting configurations, including using the main cameras for selfies or group photos while seeing the composition on the other screen. Duo FaceTime can also put nearby participants onto the outer display.

Other notable camera features include 48MP macro photography, a 2x optical-quality crop from the Main camera, an under-display inner FaceTime camera, Dual Capture for simultaneous front-and-rear video, and 4K Dolby Vision recording at up to 120fps.

Rear cameras

Britta O’Boyle/Foundry

The 48MP Fusion Main has an f/1.6 aperture, sensor-shift stabilization and can shoot 24MP or 48MP images. It also provides a 12MP, 2x optical-quality crop equivalent to a 52mm lens.

The 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide has a 13mm-equivalent lens, f/2.2 aperture and 120-degree field of view. It also supports 48MP macro photography and is the same Ultra Wide camera used by the iPhone 18 Pro family.

That means the Duo does not match the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max camera system. Those phones add a dedicated 48MP Fusion Telephoto and variable aperture on the Main camera, making the Pro models much more flexible for photography despite costing substantially less.

In his first-day testing, Macworld’s Jason Cross found the Duo’s Main camera fell behind the iPhone 18 Pro in low light, although he was pleased with the Ultra Wide camera. The Duo also lacks the Pro’s shutter-speed adjustment and histogram, while retaining white balance and manual focus with focus peaking.

Pre-event reports were divided between a Main + Telephoto and Main + Ultra Wide arrangement. Apple ultimately chose Main + Ultra Wide, confirming the earlier reports that a dedicated telephoto could be sacrificed to save space.

Front cameras

On the outside is a 12MP Center Stage camera with an f/2.2 aperture. It supports Center Stage, automatic portrait/landscape framing, Dual Capture, Photonic Engine, Deep Fusion, Smart HDR 5 and 4K Dolby Vision video at up to 60fps.

Inside is an under-display FaceTime camera with an f/1.8 aperture. Apple does not specify its megapixel resolution. It supports Center Stage for video calls and records at up to 1080p/60fps. Its major advantage is visual rather than photographic: the camera effectively disappears beneath the display when it isn’t being used.

However, image quality is a compromise. In Macworld’s testing, we found that the under-display camera produced poor detail and dynamic range. It is adequate for video calls, but for better selfies, it’s preferable to use the rear cameras with the outer display as a viewfinder.

iPhone Duo video features

The Main camera records 4K Dolby Vision at 24, 25, 30, 60, 100 or 120fps, with 4K/120fps also available for slo-mo. Cinematic mode reaches 4K/60fps and Action mode up to 2.8K/60fps. Dual Capture can record at up to 4K/30fps.

Apple’s specifications also do not list ProRes or Apple Log recording for the Duo. Those remain more Pro-oriented capabilities rather than part of Apple’s foldable camera proposition.

The Duo does support Spatial Audio recording, Audio Mix, Dolby Vision HDR and Apple’s computational photography features including Photonic Engine, Deep Fusion, Smart HDR 5, Photographic Styles 3, smart focus tracking and Apple Intelligence-powered editing.

Apple does not list conventional Spatial Video capture in the Duo specifications.

iPhone Duo processor: What processor does it use?

Apple

The iPhone Duo uses the A20 Pro, the same processor as the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.

It is manufactured using a 2-nanometer process, a major step forward in transistor density and efficiency. Apple combines it with a new chip packaging design inspired by its M-series Mac processors. The package connects the A20 Pro directly to a custom vapor chamber to transfer heat away from the processor more effectively.

The A20 Pro includes:

  • 6-core CPU: two super cores and four efficiency cores
  • 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators
  • Dual 16-core Neural Engine
  • Hardware-accelerated ray tracing
  • A dedicated display engine capable of operating both Duo displays

Compared with the A19 Pro, Apple says the CPU is up to 20 percent faster, while the GPU is up to 40 percent faster and more power-efficient. The Dual 16-core Neural Engine delivers twice the compute power, while unified-memory bandwidth rises by 50 percent.

Apple also claims that the complete thermal system gives the Duo up to 35 percent better sustained performance than the iPhone 17 Pro. That sustained-performance figure is particularly important for a folding device because prolonged gaming, multitasking and AI workloads generate considerably more heat than short benchmark bursts.

iPhone Duo RAM: How much memory does it have?

Apple has not disclosed how much RAM is inside the iPhone Duo.

Before launch, supply-chain reports consistently pointed to 12GB of RAM, which would make sense given the demands of running two displays, simultaneous applications, Siri AI and larger on-device AI models.

Apple does reveal that A20 Pro has 50 percent more unified-memory bandwidth than A19 Pro, which should help the Duo move data more quickly between the CPU, GPU and Neural Engine.

Extra memory is particularly useful on the Duo because iOS 27.1 can display multiple apps simultaneously and because Apple Intelligence and Siri AI increasingly run generative models locally rather than relying entirely on cloud processing.

iPhone Duo connectivity

Britta O’Boyle

Apple has put a significant amount of its own communications silicon into the iPhone Duo.

It uses Apple’s new C2 cellular modem, replacing Qualcomm silicon. Apple says C2 introduces AI-powered improvements to cellular quality and reliability and supports mmWave 5G in the U.S.

The N1 wireless networking chip provides:

  • Wi-Fi 7 with 2×2 MIMO
  • Bluetooth 6
  • Thread networking

The USB-C port also supports USB 3 data transfers at up to 10Gbps and DisplayPort video output.

The Duo also has Apple’s second-generation Ultra Wideband chip, NFC and precision dual-frequency GPS.

It is eSIM-only worldwide, something that had been widely rumored before launch. Eliminating the SIM tray gives Apple additional internal space for its batteries.

iPhone Handoff – a feature introduced with iOS 27 – makes it easier to use an iPhone Duo alongside another iPhone without needing separate phone numbers. Both devices share your number, with calls, voicemail, messages and Find My location following whichever iPhone you unlock. Only one phone is active at a time. You could use the Duo’s folding display for work, then switch to an iPhone Pro when you want its telephoto camera. Both phones need iOS 27, eSIM support and the same Apple Account, with Messages in iCloud enabled. Your carrier must specifically support iPhone Handoff, and your plan may require an additional monthly fee for access. T-Mobile already offers iPhone Handoff for $5 a month; Verizon and EE (in the U.K.) plan support. Fees may apply.

Satellite capabilities include:

  • Emergency SOS via satellite
  • Roadside Assistance via satellite
  • Find My via satellite
  • Messages via satellite

Battery, MagSafe and charging: What’s available?

Instead of one battery spanning the body, the iPhone Duo contains two rechargeable lithium-ion batteries, with one high-energy battery fitted into each half of the device. Apple’s energy-balancing algorithms make them operate as a single battery system.

Apple rates battery life at:

  • Up to 24 hours of typical use
  • Up to 44 hours video playback using the outer display
  • Up to 31 hours using the inner display
  • Up to 37 hours streamed video on the outer screen
  • Up to 26 hours streamed video on the inner display

Early reviewers reported different battery experiences. CNET found the Duo comfortably lasted through a busy day, while The Verge questioned whether it could manage a full day of heavy use. These observations reflect different usage patterns and testing methods, so they should not be treated as directly comparable results or replacements for Apple’s playback ratings above.

After using the Duo as her main phone for a week, Macworld contributor Britta O’Boyle generally finished her mixed-use days with around 25 percent battery remaining. In her experience, it outlasted the smaller iPhone 18 Pro but fell slightly short of the Pro Max. These are everyday-use observations rather than directly comparable laboratory benchmarks.

Apple has not disclosed the batteries’ combined capacity in mAh. The pre-launch rumor of approximately 5,000-5,500mAh therefore remains unconfirmed.

Apple says the iPhone Duo can reach 50 percent charge in around 20 minutes using a USB-C charging cable and a 60W-capable power adapter or higher.

Britta O’Boyle’s charging test broadly matched Apple’s claim: using a 60W adapter, she reached approximately 50 percent from empty in around 20 minutes.

Our iPhone Duo reviewer, Jason Cross, found that battery life depended heavily on which display he used. Frequent gaming or video editing on the inner screen could require charging by mid-afternoon, while more folded use left plenty of charge at bedtime. Unfortunately, Macworld’s standard battery benchmark app crashed on launch, so his review contains no directly comparable laboratory battery result.

MagSafe and Qi2 wireless charging are supported at up to 25W. Apple’s claimed 50 percent charge in around 30 minutes requires a MagSafe charger paired with a 35W-or-higher power adapter.

In both the U.S. and U.K., the box includes the iPhone Duo and a 1-meter USB-C charging cable, but no power adapter. The MagSafe charger is also sold separately, so factor these accessories into your budget if you don’t already own suitable equipment.

iPhone Duo price: How much does it cost?

The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 in the U.S. and £1,999 in the U.K. for 256GB.

Prices are:

The 256GB starting capacity means Apple has not created an unusually low-storage entry model simply to make the headline price look lower.

iPhone Duo vs iPhone 18 Pro pricing

The iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199/£1,199, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at $1,299/£1,299. That makes the Duo approximately $700/£700 more expensive than the Pro Max at entry level.

That premium buys the folding display, precision hinge, titanium structure, second screen and more complex dual-battery design rather than superior cameras: in several areas the iPhone 18 Pro models are actually better equipped.

Reports before the launch suggested the Duo could cost anywhere from around $1,999 to $2,399 at entry level, largely because of the folding OLED display, hinge mechanism, titanium components and other expensive parts. Apple ultimately landed at the very bottom of those predictions.

iPhone Duo software: Multitasking and Apple Pencil support

Britta O’Boyle

The iPhone Duo’s larger inner display enables Split View, letting you use two apps side by side. For example, you could keep Safari open while taking notes, or check your calendar alongside a conversation in Messages. Supported apps can also open two windows of their own: Safari can display two webpages side by side for comparison shopping. You can save pairs of apps to return to later.

App compatibility varies considerably. Macworld’s Jason Cross identified three broad experiences: older apps with fixed layouts and black borders; apps updated for iOS 27 that resize across the displays; and fully Duo-optimized apps that adapt to its different positions. After some initial issues, Outlook has been updated and now has a Duo-optimized layout that makes better use of the inner display.

App support is improving, however. Netflix, Fantastical, MLB and Asphalt Legends were among the apps Apple highlighted at launch, and optimized apps carry a “Made for iPhone Duo“ badge on their App Store product pages. You can also consult the crowdsourced Works on Duo database to check how individual apps use the Duo’s displays before buying.

StandBy also works differently on the Duo. Set the phone down and it can display a clock, photos or widgets on either screen without being connected to a charger. New Calendar and Weather faces join the existing options.

Apple Pencil (USB-C) support arrived with iOS 27.2 on October 26, allowing users to write, sketch and mark up documents on either display. Update through Settings > General > Software Update to access the feature.

The update also adds Edge Light, which uses the display to illuminate your face during video calls. Other iOS 27.2 additions include improvements to Siri AI’s conversation recall and personal context, plus contextual Suggestions in Messages. Read our guide to the iOS 27.2 update.

iPhone Duo review: What did Macworld think?

In Macworld’s full iPhone Duo review, Jason Cross praises the nano-texture inner display, fast performance and thoughtful layouts in optimized apps.

However, many everyday apps remain awkward to use, while the cameras and Touch ID introduce further compromises.

Our verdict: An exciting device to explore, but one he cannot yet recommend buying.

Should you buy the iPhone Duo?

Britta O’Boyle

Our advice is to wait, principally because too many popular apps still work poorly on the Duo. Before buying an iPhone Duo, check whether the apps you rely on have layouts designed for its displays.

Additionally, at $1,999/£1,999 it is enormously expensive, and there are significant compromises: no Face ID, no dedicated telephoto camera, no variable aperture and no Action button. 

Durability is another consideration. On October 26, Apple acknowledged an inner-display issue affecting a small number of iPhone Duo units and advised affected customers to contact AppleCare for a replacement. The cause and failure rate remain unclear. If first-generation reliability concerns you, consider waiting for further investigation and longer-term testing before spending $1,999/£1,999.

For photography, battery life and conventional everyday use, the better-value iPhone 18 Pro Max is the best iPhone.

Apple Inventory Check monitors Apple Store availability in various countries, including the U.S. and U.K., while TrackaLacker covers selected online retailers, including Best Buy and Walmart. Some notification features require registration or payment.

Apple described preorder demand as “nothing short of extraordinary” and said it was working to get devices to customers as quickly as possible.

Supply constraints may also contribute to the backlog. A late-September report claimed that Apple and its manufacturing partners were experiencing low production yields. Long delivery waits therefore reflect the balance between demand and available supply, rather than revealing how many phones Apple has sold.

iPhone Duo design: What does it look like?

Britta O’Boyle/Foundry

The iPhone Duo uses a book-style folding design. Closed, it is unusually short and wide for an iPhone, measuring 84.1mm wide, 117.8mm tall and 11.3mm thick. Open it and the width expands to 164.6mm, while thickness reduces to just 5.2mm, making it Apple’s thinnest iPhone when unfolded (taking that mantle from the iPhone Air). It weighs 254g.

The outer screen measures 5.4 inches, while the folding inner panel measures 7.6 inches. Both are Super Retina XDR OLED displays with ProMotion up to 120Hz, Always-On display support and up to 3,000 nits outdoor peak brightness. The internal display also has a nano-texture surface designed to reduce reflections and make the crease less noticeable. The inner display also has a replaceable top cover layer.

According to iFixit’s report on Apple’s U.S. repair pricing, replacing the inner screen’s cover layer costs $49 without AppleCare+, or a $19 service fee with AppleCare+. This replaces only the top cover layer. Repairing damage to the inner display itself costs substantially more: $999 without AppleCare+, or a $99 service fee with AppleCare+. If damage is experienced and found to be a manufacturing fault, Apple may accept the device for repair under warranty at no cost.

The frame and hinge cover are made from Grade 5 titanium. Apple uses a mirror-polished finish on the enclosure and a micro-blasted finish on the 3D-printed hinge cover. Ceramic Shield protects the rear, while Ceramic Shield 2 protects the outer display. The phone retains an IP68 rating despite its folding construction.

Britta O’Boyle/Foundry

There are just two colors: Star White and Night Sky, essentially confirming the pre-event reports of silver/white and a very dark blue. For more information read about the iPhone Duo colors.

Action button and Camera Control

There is Camera Control, giving access to exposure, depth, zoom, cameras, styles and tone. It can also launch the new Siri Camera mode.

However, Apple’s Duo doesn’t feature an Action button. The regular iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max retain both the Action button and Camera Control, so this is one hardware-control compromise of the folding model.

Accessories

Apple is also launching two dedicated accessories for the foldable:

  • The iPhone Duo Case at $79/£79
  • The Duo Folio with Kickstand at $129/£129

Apple’s standard case leaves the hinge exposed, while the Folio with Kickstand provides hinge protection.

Both became available to order on October 16. And there are plenty more of the best cases for iPhone Duo in our test reviews.

iPhone Duo problems: Screen cracks and hinge concerns

Some early iPhone Duo owners have reported cracks along the inner display’s fold, sometimes accompanied by bright lines across the screen. One Australian owner said the damage appeared after around six hours and fewer than 20 openings, and reported receiving an immediate replacement at an Apple Store. These are owner reports; the cause and extent of the problem remain unclear.

Apple acknowledged the issue on October 26, saying it affects a small number of iPhone Duo units. The company advises customers experiencing inner-display problems to contact AppleCare for a replacement. Apple has not announced a formal repair program or confirmed the underlying cause. As reported on November 2, Apple has also circulated diagnostic guidance to Apple Stores and Apple Authorized Service Providers. Read our report on the Duo’s display and hinge problems.

iFixit’s teardown offers a possible explanation: its 3D hinge model places reported damage near a transition between the flex-cable opening and central display support. One simulation shows how a support that fails to retract sufficiently could press against the folding screen.

Apple published an iPhone Duo hinge troubleshooting guide on October 23. It covers devices that do not open or close fully, unexpected noises, loose or damaged hinges, and enclosure damage affecting the mechanism.

Apple says there are no software remedies for hinge problems, so restarting, updating or restoring the phone is unnecessary. Its service procedure calls for inspection and, if the problem remains unresolved, replacement of the inner display assembly. Owners experiencing problems should contact Apple or an authorized service provider for assessment.

How repairable is the iPhone Duo?

iFixit awarded the Duo a provisional repairability score of 5/10, its highest for a foldable at the time. It praised the removable outer display and electrically released batteries, but found inner-display and hinge repairs difficult. The score reflects some accessible components, but is provisional pending replacement-parts availability.

Its fluorescent-powder experiment also found particles reaching the hinge, but this does not establish the cause of owners’ screen failures.

Face ID, Touch ID and the notch

Britta O’Boyle/Foundry

Perhaps the most surprising difference between the iPhone Duo and Apple’s other flagship iPhones is that there is no Face ID.

Instead, Apple has brought back Touch ID, with the fingerprint sensor incorporated into the side button. It works whether the Duo is folded or unfolded, and Apple Watch can also be used to unlock the device. This confirms one of the most persistent pre-launch rumors.

The internal display therefore does not need the TrueDepth sensors used for Face ID. Its FaceTime camera sits beneath the display and disappears when it isn’t being used, giving the inner screen a largely uninterrupted surface.

The inner camera itself is hidden below the display rather than sitting permanently in a visible camera cutout. And yet, despite this and the absence of Face ID, there is still support for Dynamic Island.

Future Duo models could restore Face ID. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Apple has tested iPhone Duo 2 prototypes with an under-display Face ID sensor and camera on the outer screen. However, he suggests the technology could arrive with either the second or third generation, so its inclusion in the next model remains uncertain.

iPhone Duo cameras: What cameras does it have?

Britta O’Boyle/Foundry

The Duo has a 48MP Dual Fusion camera system, comprising:

The Duo does not have variable aperture. Variable aperture is exclusive to the 48MP Fusion Main camera in the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.

The biggest camera features for iPhone Duo

Duo Preview

The outer screen can show a live preview while somebody else is being photographed, allowing the subject to adjust their pose and framing.

Smart Take and Kid Cue

Smart Take detects when everybody is ready and automatically captures the shot. Kid Cue uses animations on the outer screen to encourage children to look towards the camera.

Two-screen shooting

The folding design supports unusual shooting configurations, including using the main cameras for selfies or group photos while seeing the composition on the other screen. Duo FaceTime can also put nearby participants onto the outer display.

Other notable camera features include 48MP macro photography, a 2x optical-quality crop from the Main camera, an under-display inner FaceTime camera, Dual Capture for simultaneous front-and-rear video, and 4K Dolby Vision recording at up to 120fps.

Rear cameras

Britta O’Boyle/Foundry

The 48MP Fusion Main has an f/1.6 aperture, sensor-shift stabilization and can shoot 24MP or 48MP images. It also provides a 12MP, 2x optical-quality crop equivalent to a 52mm lens.

The 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide has a 13mm-equivalent lens, f/2.2 aperture and 120-degree field of view. It also supports 48MP macro photography and is the same Ultra Wide camera used by the iPhone 18 Pro family.

That means the Duo does not match the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max camera system. Those phones add a dedicated 48MP Fusion Telephoto and variable aperture on the Main camera, making the Pro models much more flexible for photography despite costing substantially less.

In his first-day testing, Macworld’s Jason Cross found the Duo’s Main camera fell behind the iPhone 18 Pro in low light, although he was pleased with the Ultra Wide camera. The Duo also lacks the Pro’s shutter-speed adjustment and histogram, while retaining white balance and manual focus with focus peaking.

Pre-event reports were divided between a Main + Telephoto and Main + Ultra Wide arrangement. Apple ultimately chose Main + Ultra Wide, confirming the earlier reports that a dedicated telephoto could be sacrificed to save space.

Front cameras

On the outside is a 12MP Center Stage camera with an f/2.2 aperture. It supports Center Stage, automatic portrait/landscape framing, Dual Capture, Photonic Engine, Deep Fusion, Smart HDR 5 and 4K Dolby Vision video at up to 60fps.

Inside is an under-display FaceTime camera with an f/1.8 aperture. Apple does not specify its megapixel resolution. It supports Center Stage for video calls and records at up to 1080p/60fps. Its major advantage is visual rather than photographic: the camera effectively disappears beneath the display when it isn’t being used.

However, image quality is a compromise. In Macworld’s testing, we found that the under-display camera produced poor detail and dynamic range. It is adequate for video calls, but for better selfies, it’s preferable to use the rear cameras with the outer display as a viewfinder.

iPhone Duo video features

The Main camera records 4K Dolby Vision at 24, 25, 30, 60, 100 or 120fps, with 4K/120fps also available for slo-mo. Cinematic mode reaches 4K/60fps and Action mode up to 2.8K/60fps. Dual Capture can record at up to 4K/30fps.

Apple’s specifications also do not list ProRes or Apple Log recording for the Duo. Those remain more Pro-oriented capabilities rather than part of Apple’s foldable camera proposition.

The Duo does support Spatial Audio recording, Audio Mix, Dolby Vision HDR and Apple’s computational photography features including Photonic Engine, Deep Fusion, Smart HDR 5, Photographic Styles 3, smart focus tracking and Apple Intelligence-powered editing.

Apple does not list conventional Spatial Video capture in the Duo specifications.

iPhone Duo processor: What processor does it use?

Apple

The iPhone Duo uses the A20 Pro, the same processor as the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.

It is manufactured using a 2-nanometer process, a major step forward in transistor density and efficiency. Apple combines it with a new chip packaging design inspired by its M-series Mac processors. The package connects the A20 Pro directly to a custom vapor chamber to transfer heat away from the processor more effectively.

The A20 Pro includes:

  • 6-core CPU: two super cores and four efficiency cores
  • 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators
  • Dual 16-core Neural Engine
  • Hardware-accelerated ray tracing
  • A dedicated display engine capable of operating both Duo displays

Compared with the A19 Pro, Apple says the CPU is up to 20 percent faster, while the GPU is up to 40 percent faster and more power-efficient. The Dual 16-core Neural Engine delivers twice the compute power, while unified-memory bandwidth rises by 50 percent.

Apple also claims that the complete thermal system gives the Duo up to 35 percent better sustained performance than the iPhone 17 Pro. That sustained-performance figure is particularly important for a folding device because prolonged gaming, multitasking and AI workloads generate considerably more heat than short benchmark bursts.

iPhone Duo RAM: How much memory does it have?

Apple has not disclosed how much RAM is inside the iPhone Duo.

Before launch, supply-chain reports consistently pointed to 12GB of RAM, which would make sense given the demands of running two displays, simultaneous applications, Siri AI and larger on-device AI models.

Apple does reveal that A20 Pro has 50 percent more unified-memory bandwidth than A19 Pro, which should help the Duo move data more quickly between the CPU, GPU and Neural Engine.

Extra memory is particularly useful on the Duo because iOS 27.1 can display multiple apps simultaneously and because Apple Intelligence and Siri AI increasingly run generative models locally rather than relying entirely on cloud processing.

iPhone Duo connectivity

Britta O’Boyle

Apple has put a significant amount of its own communications silicon into the iPhone Duo.

It uses Apple’s new C2 cellular modem, replacing Qualcomm silicon. Apple says C2 introduces AI-powered improvements to cellular quality and reliability and supports mmWave 5G in the U.S.

The N1 wireless networking chip provides:

  • Wi-Fi 7 with 2×2 MIMO
  • Bluetooth 6
  • Thread networking

The USB-C port also supports USB 3 data transfers at up to 10Gbps and DisplayPort video output.

The Duo also has Apple’s second-generation Ultra Wideband chip, NFC and precision dual-frequency GPS.

It is eSIM-only worldwide, something that had been widely rumored before launch. Eliminating the SIM tray gives Apple additional internal space for its batteries.

iPhone Handoff – a feature introduced with iOS 27 – makes it easier to use an iPhone Duo alongside another iPhone without needing separate phone numbers. Both devices share your number, with calls, voicemail, messages and Find My location following whichever iPhone you unlock. Only one phone is active at a time. You could use the Duo’s folding display for work, then switch to an iPhone Pro when you want its telephoto camera. Both phones need iOS 27, eSIM support and the same Apple Account, with Messages in iCloud enabled. Your carrier must specifically support iPhone Handoff, and your plan may require an additional monthly fee for access. T-Mobile already offers iPhone Handoff for $5 a month; Verizon and EE (in the U.K.) plan support. Fees may apply.

Satellite capabilities include:

  • Emergency SOS via satellite
  • Roadside Assistance via satellite
  • Find My via satellite
  • Messages via satellite

Battery, MagSafe and charging: What’s available?

Instead of one battery spanning the body, the iPhone Duo contains two rechargeable lithium-ion batteries, with one high-energy battery fitted into each half of the device. Apple’s energy-balancing algorithms make them operate as a single battery system.

Apple rates battery life at:

  • Up to 24 hours of typical use
  • Up to 44 hours video playback using the outer display
  • Up to 31 hours using the inner display
  • Up to 37 hours streamed video on the outer screen
  • Up to 26 hours streamed video on the inner display

Early reviewers reported different battery experiences. CNET found the Duo comfortably lasted through a busy day, while The Verge questioned whether it could manage a full day of heavy use. These observations reflect different usage patterns and testing methods, so they should not be treated as directly comparable results or replacements for Apple’s playback ratings above.

After using the Duo as her main phone for a week, Macworld contributor Britta O’Boyle generally finished her mixed-use days with around 25 percent battery remaining. In her experience, it outlasted the smaller iPhone 18 Pro but fell slightly short of the Pro Max. These are everyday-use observations rather than directly comparable laboratory benchmarks.

Apple has not disclosed the batteries’ combined capacity in mAh. The pre-launch rumor of approximately 5,000-5,500mAh therefore remains unconfirmed.

Apple says the iPhone Duo can reach 50 percent charge in around 20 minutes using a USB-C charging cable and a 60W-capable power adapter or higher.

Britta O’Boyle’s charging test broadly matched Apple’s claim: using a 60W adapter, she reached approximately 50 percent from empty in around 20 minutes.

Our iPhone Duo reviewer, Jason Cross, found that battery life depended heavily on which display he used. Frequent gaming or video editing on the inner screen could require charging by mid-afternoon, while more folded use left plenty of charge at bedtime. Unfortunately, Macworld’s standard battery benchmark app crashed on launch, so his review contains no directly comparable laboratory battery result.

MagSafe and Qi2 wireless charging are supported at up to 25W. Apple’s claimed 50 percent charge in around 30 minutes requires a MagSafe charger paired with a 35W-or-higher power adapter.

In both the U.S. and U.K., the box includes the iPhone Duo and a 1-meter USB-C charging cable, but no power adapter. The MagSafe charger is also sold separately, so factor these accessories into your budget if you don’t already own suitable equipment.

iPhone Duo price: How much does it cost?

The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 in the U.S. and £1,999 in the U.K. for 256GB.

Prices are:

The 256GB starting capacity means Apple has not created an unusually low-storage entry model simply to make the headline price look lower.

iPhone Duo vs iPhone 18 Pro pricing

The iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199/£1,199, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at $1,299/£1,299. That makes the Duo approximately $700/£700 more expensive than the Pro Max at entry level.

That premium buys the folding display, precision hinge, titanium structure, second screen and more complex dual-battery design rather than superior cameras: in several areas the iPhone 18 Pro models are actually better equipped.

Reports before the launch suggested the Duo could cost anywhere from around $1,999 to $2,399 at entry level, largely because of the folding OLED display, hinge mechanism, titanium components and other expensive parts. Apple ultimately landed at the very bottom of those predictions.

iPhone Duo software: Multitasking and Apple Pencil support

Britta O’Boyle

The iPhone Duo’s larger inner display enables Split View, letting you use two apps side by side. For example, you could keep Safari open while taking notes, or check your calendar alongside a conversation in Messages. Supported apps can also open two windows of their own: Safari can display two webpages side by side for comparison shopping. You can save pairs of apps to return to later.

App compatibility varies considerably. Macworld’s Jason Cross identified three broad experiences: older apps with fixed layouts and black borders; apps updated for iOS 27 that resize across the displays; and fully Duo-optimized apps that adapt to its different positions. After some initial issues, Outlook has been updated and now has a Duo-optimized layout that makes better use of the inner display.

App support is improving, however. Netflix, Fantastical, MLB and Asphalt Legends were among the apps Apple highlighted at launch, and optimized apps carry a “Made for iPhone Duo“ badge on their App Store product pages. You can also consult the crowdsourced Works on Duo database to check how individual apps use the Duo’s displays before buying.

StandBy also works differently on the Duo. Set the phone down and it can display a clock, photos or widgets on either screen without being connected to a charger. New Calendar and Weather faces join the existing options.

Apple Pencil (USB-C) support arrived with iOS 27.2 on October 26, allowing users to write, sketch and mark up documents on either display. Update through Settings > General > Software Update to access the feature.

The update also adds Edge Light, which uses the display to illuminate your face during video calls. Other iOS 27.2 additions include improvements to Siri AI’s conversation recall and personal context, plus contextual Suggestions in Messages. Read our guide to the iOS 27.2 update.

iPhone Duo review: What did Macworld think?

In Macworld’s full iPhone Duo review, Jason Cross praises the nano-texture inner display, fast performance and thoughtful layouts in optimized apps.

However, many everyday apps remain awkward to use, while the cameras and Touch ID introduce further compromises.

Our verdict: An exciting device to explore, but one he cannot yet recommend buying.

Should you buy the iPhone Duo?

Britta O’Boyle

Our advice is to wait, principally because too many popular apps still work poorly on the Duo. Before buying an iPhone Duo, check whether the apps you rely on have layouts designed for its displays.

Additionally, at $1,999/£1,999 it is enormously expensive, and there are significant compromises: no Face ID, no dedicated telephoto camera, no variable aperture and no Action button. 

Durability is another consideration. On October 26, Apple acknowledged an inner-display issue affecting a small number of iPhone Duo units and advised affected customers to contact AppleCare for a replacement. The cause and failure rate remain unclear. If first-generation reliability concerns you, consider waiting for further investigation and longer-term testing before spending $1,999/£1,999.

For photography, battery life and conventional everyday use, the better-value iPhone 18 Pro Max is the best iPhone.

The Finder in macOS is where you spend the most time when using your Mac. It is the most important tool for managing files and folders; it’s the basis for installing and launching apps; it’s where you can manage iPhones and iPads; and a lot more. It’s the foundation for the macOS interface and for using your Mac hardware.

Many Mac users have been using the Finder every day for decades, often without making full use of its capabilities or customizing it to suit their own needs. You should make the most of your UI experience. Here are ten tips on how to get more out of the Finder.

Customize the toolbar

This is a very simple thing to do, but hardly anyone does. You should adjust the Finder toolbar to suit your own needs. To do this, open a Finder window and right-click on the toolbar. You’ll see the Customize Toolbar option in the context menu. Select it, and a window will appear with additional functions and tools. You can click and drag icons to where you want them in the toolbar.

The AirDrop icon, for example, is useful if you transfer files often: once it’s been added to the Finder, you simply select an item and send it straight away. The buttons for burning blank discs, ejecting media, and accessing servers can also be useful, depending on your needs.

Foundry

You can also easily change the order of the icons. Simply click on one while holding down the Command key. To remove it from the toolbar, simply drag it out.

Quick Commands for photo editing and your own scripts

Quick Actions are small tools that you can access via the context menu (the menu that appears when you right-click an item). They allow you to quickly convert PNG to JPEG or create a PDF, for example.

Six system services are provided by default, though the options available in the context menu depend on the selected file type. For example, if you right-click on a video, you can access a function to trim the video. This is quicker and easier than using QuickTime Player.

For photos, you can quickly convert them to other formats such as JPEG; you can combine several PDFs into a single PDF file using Create PDF; rotate a photo; and remove the background from a photo (though this doesn’t always work). For image files and PDFs, there’s also the option to add annotations. This opens a window with the tools familiar from Preview, allowing you to add lines, red arrows, and other annotations.

Foundry

You can enable and disable these useful extensions under General > Login Items & Extensions > System Services. To do this, click on the ‘i’ icon there.

There’s even a way to add your own Quick Actions: to do this, simply select ‘Quick Action’ as the file type in Automator and create a workflow – such as resizing a photo to a specific width. Once created, the workflow is immediately available via the context menu.

Rename multiple files

You don’t need to resort to a tool like Renamer to rename dozens of files or folders. The Finder also has a built-in function for renaming files. However, it’s somewhat hidden.

To access the feature, select multiple files and choose Rename from the context menu. If you selected just a single file, you can only change the name within the Finder; the file will be selected for you automatically. However, if you’ve selected multiple files, a separate new window opens with several options.

Foundry

Here you can choose from several renaming options; you can add text, replace text, or rename all files according to a new format. When replacing text, simply enter the original text and the new text in the two fields. When adding text, you can choose to add it at the beginning or the end, as a prefix or suffix.

The Format option is more complex, offering three choices: here you can choose between two numbering styles and adding the current date.

Manage the clipboards

Starting with macOS Tahoe, old clipboard contents can be saved by the system on request and are searchable via Spotlight. You’ll need to enable this feature first via the Spotlight system setting. You can also select a retention period; options are 8 hours, 30 minutes, and 7 days.

Once enabled, you can enter a search term into Spotlight to search the clipboard text. Alongside other results, you’ll then see a list of previous clipboard entries, marked with two small boxes. You can also press Command+4 or select Clipboard after opening Spotlight.

You can valso iew the current clipboard select Edit > Show Clipboard from the menu bar in Finder, and the current clipboard will be displayed in a simple window.

Foundry

Hide all items on the Desktop

Apple now offers so many options for the Desktop and Dock that some people lose track of them all. For a long time, I overlooked the fact that the Desktop & Dock system setting can hide all items on the desktop completely.

To do this, go to the Desktop & Dock system settings and, under Show items, untick the box next to On the Desktop. You can later show all folders and files again using the same function.

Foundry

List invisible files and folders

The Mac actually has countless invisible folders and files on your system. Most are used by the system and are best left hidden, otherwise, your folders can quickly become cluttered. Sometimes, invisible files are left behind when you uninstall an app or delete a file.

All you need to do is press Command+Shift+. to see invisible files. The first time you press the key combination, you see all hidden files and folders in the selected folder. Press it again, and they’ll disappear again.

Hide files or folders

You can make a file or folder invisible via Terminal: enter the command chflags hidden and add the path–drag and drop the file or folder into the Terminal window to do this.

Connect to a server

The Finder is also responsible for allowing you to connect via the network: to other Macs, the company server or even a Fritzbox with NAS functionality. Available servers are often listed automatically in the Finder under Network. You can connect manually via Go > Connect to Server.

Even FTP is supported, but you can only download data. Uploads are not possible, and FTP servers using the SFTP or FTPS protocols are not supported. However, the FTP function is not always reliable and has often caused problems. It is not without reason that many experienced users prefer to use an FTP client such as Cyberduck for every FTP connection.

Make better use of Smart Folders

Smart Folders are very powerful, but unfortunately can be too fiddly. These ingenious folders are essentially saved search queries that update dynamically. You can save these folders once created and conveniently pin them to the sidebar. By default, however, the Finder links all search criteria using only simple AND conditions, as is familiar from Spotlight or the Google search engine.

Foundry

But the folder becomes truly smart with so-called Boolean operators. For example, when you’re looking for all image files but also all video files, or all files that are neither image files nor video files. (This might sound like a fiddly logic puzzle to you right now, but it can be very useful!)

Apple has hidden this option a little, presumably so as not to overwhelm beginners. First, create a smart folder as usual, for example, via File > New Smart Folder. Then click the + icon, and you can define the criteria for the items you want to appear in the folder. Click the + icon to add more definitions. Click the Save button to set the Smart Folder, and then when you open the folder, it will show all the items that fit the criteria you defined.

The Finder is also responsible for allowing you to connect via the network: to other Macs, the company server or even a Fritzbox with NAS functionality. Available servers are often listed automatically in the Finder under Network. You can connect manually via Go > Connect to Server.

Even FTP is supported, but you can only download data. Uploads are not possible, and FTP servers using the SFTP or FTPS protocols are not supported. However, the FTP function is not always reliable and has often caused problems. It is not without reason that many experienced users prefer to use an FTP client such as Cyberduck for every FTP connection.

Make better use of Smart Folders

Smart Folders are very powerful, but unfortunately can be too fiddly. These ingenious folders are essentially saved search queries that update dynamically. You can save these folders once created and conveniently pin them to the sidebar. By default, however, the Finder links all search criteria using only simple AND conditions, as is familiar from Spotlight or the Google search engine.

Foundry

But the folder becomes truly smart with so-called Boolean operators. For example, when you’re looking for all image files but also all video files, or all files that are neither image files nor video files. (This might sound like a fiddly logic puzzle to you right now, but it can be very useful!)

Apple has hidden this option a little, presumably so as not to overwhelm beginners. First, create a smart folder as usual, for example, via File > New Smart Folder. Then click the + icon, and you can define the criteria for the items you want to appear in the folder. Click the + icon to add more definitions. Click the Save button to set the Smart Folder, and then when you open the folder, it will show all the items that fit the criteria you defined.
